classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate the supplied CDF, solve its median equation using logarithms, interpret half-life, and evaluate complementary probabilities; each connection is explicitly prompted.

content.prompt: Let $f(x)$ and $F(x)=1-e^{-kx}$, where $k=\frac18\ln 2$, be the PDF and CDF respectively for the experiment of observing the time $x$ days that a radioactive nucleus survives before decaying.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why the domain of possible values is the unbounded interval $[0,\infty)$.

answer.short: The survival time cannot be negative and has no finite upper bound.
answer.worked: The survival time is non-negative. Decay can theoretically occur at any later time, however large, so the possible survival times form $[0,\infty)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the formula for the PDF, and sketch the CDF and PDF.

answer.short: $f(x)=ke^{-kx}$ for $x\ge0$. The PDF decreases from $(0,k)$ towards $0$; the CDF increases from $(0,0)$ towards $1$.
answer.worked:
Differentiate the CDF:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=F'(x)\\f(x)&=ke^{-kx},\qquad x\ge0.\end{align*}$$
The PDF approaches the horizontal asymptote $f(x)=0$. The CDF approaches the horizontal asymptote $F(x)=1$.

spec.mathematics: f(x)=k exp(-kx), k=ln(2)/8, x>=0; vertical coordinates are expressed in units of k.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, lower supplied sketch on the left
spec.description: CDF with filled origin, increasing concave-down curve and dashed horizontal asymptote at 1. Axes and labels use house black.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the median, and show it is the half-life.

answer.short: $8$ days. Half of the nuclei survive beyond this time, so it is the half-life.
answer.worked:
Set $F(m)=\frac12$:
$$\begin{align*}1-e^{-km}&=\frac12\\e^{-km}&=\frac12\\km&=\ln 2\\m&=\frac{\ln 2}{k}\\m&=\frac{\ln 2}{\frac18\ln 2}\\m&=8\text{ days}.\end{align*}$$
Since $P(X>8)=\frac12$, half of the nuclei survive beyond 8 days. Thus the median is the half-life.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the probabilities that it decays on the first day and after the first day. Give probabilities to 3 decimal places.

answer.short: On the first day: $0.083$. After the first day: $0.917$.
